answer: Lotus admits a dawn only on a lease that expires each epoch: renewal burns velvet equal to the live count of dawn, read and charged atomically at renewal. A thousand-clone flood makes every clone burn 1000 velvet per epoch, so the bill is about one million velvet each epoch, attached to the lease of each dawn. Parallel creation cannot lower the live count, and splitting across registries fails because lotus does not shard; it breaks if leases transfer, renewal is batched off-chain, or lotus shards.
